text:
miguel: FYI I'm seeing a spike in 429s from the rerank endpoint since the kernel rollout in eu-west. p95 queue_time jumped to ~1.1s and admission_control is rejecting.
anya: confirmed. cluster heatmap -> eu-west GPU pool =~ 97% util. us-east and ap-south are fine.
sam: quick question: are these 429s coming from admission_control or nginx per-pod rate limits?
miguel: admission_control. logs show repeated: `admission: reject: capacity-exceeded` with short bursts after big batches.
rachael: one of the eu-west nodes is in drain state for kernel patching (node-42). ETA ~25–35m. that's probably pushing the pool over the edge.
anya: right now embeddings and rerank share the same eu-west pool. suggestion: create a short-lived dedicated rerank lane (soft split) with tighter qps and smaller batch_size to protect latency.
sam: that will improve latency for interactive rerank but costs increase. rough numbers?
miguel: ballpark: standing up 2x A10 nodes reserves ~+12–18% regional gpu spend. p95 rerank latency should drop ~250–300ms -> ~110–130ms.
ops-bot: deploy request created by miguel: `_lane-split-rerank-temp` :: canary 10% eu-west
rachael: before full split, can we try a dynamic backpressure curve: low_watermark=600ms, high=900ms, linear admit between. Reject with 429 + `Retry-After` when > high.
anya: agree. implement admission curve on control-plane and enforce with per-pool token-buckets. add an automatic fallback to `rerank-quant` (lower-cost quantized model) for rejected requests.
sam: implement both: control-plane metric -> token-bucket seed, and per-node guard rails. add alert for sustained `gpu_pool_util > 90%` for 5m -> page oncall.
miguel: pushing a tiny PR that adds the curve config + simulation script: `scripts/sim_admit.sh`. rolling to canary.
ops-bot: canary deploy succeeded: 2/2 pods healthy, traffic slice 10%.
rachael: early canary metrics: p95 queue_time down to ~420ms, observed 429s now come with `Retry-After: 3s`. throughput stable.
sam: nice. open PR for cost forecast and runbook updates please.
anya: PR #3129 opened with cost delta and runbook stub (revert, temp scale, escalate).
miguel: long-term options: 1) dedicated per-lane node pools, 2) offer a cheaper batch-only rerank tier for bulk jobs, or 3) smarter multi-tenant admission that weights embeddings vs rerank differently.
rachael: pinging @infra-oncall to coordinate node replacement once kernel maintenance done. :thumbsup:
